e: "But she can meet you tomorrow" shows she cannot meet now: unavailable = not free.

q: Learning to swim was hard for Omar, but his coach told him to stick with it. She meant that he should ______.
e: Stick with (or to) it = keep trying, do not give up.

q: Several soldiers in my unit are ______ in taking the advanced language course.
e: Use the -ed adjective for a person's feeling: interested in + -ing.

q: By the end of this month, every vehicle in the motor pool ______ for winter driving.
e: Future perfect passive (will have been + past participle): the vehicles receive the action before a future time.

q: Have you heard ______ your old roommate since he moved to Alaska?
e: Hear from someone = get news, a call or a letter from them.

q: Our supply clerk never forgets an order; everyone in the office knows they can ______ her.
e: Count on someone = depend on them, trust them to help.

q: Early ships depended on the wind. Steam engines later made them faster. Now most large ships burn diesel, which lets them travel much farther. According to this paragraph, modern ships ______.
o: still depend mainly on the wind
are slower than the old steamships
e: The text says most large ships now burn diesel.

q: Never run a generator in a closed garage; the poisonous ______ from its engine can kill you quickly.
e: Fumes = harmful gas or smoke, such as engine exhaust.

q: Our company has ______ trucks than the company next door, so they often borrow ours.
e: Use more + noun + than to compare two groups; the most is for three or more.

q: "______ time does the mail truck usually reach the barracks?" "Around ten o'clock."
e: Ask about the clock with the question What time...?

q: Excuse me, sergeant, we are waiting outside the auditorium. Do you know ______?
o: how long the briefing will last
how long will the briefing last
how long does the briefing last
how long will last the briefing
e: After "do you know" use statement word order: how long + subject + verb.

q: Because the base is far from town, many families rely on the shuttle bus for ______ to the shopping center.
e: Transportation means a way of getting from one place to another.

q: The police recovered the ______ laptop from a pawn shop and returned it to its owner.
e: A past participle (stolen) can work as an adjective: a laptop that was stolen.

q: Good afternoon, sir. ______ we leave our bags here while we check in?
e: Use May + subject + base verb to ask politely for permission.

q: The wounded hikers ______ by helicopter early this morning.
e: Passive past (were + past participle): the hikers received the action.

q: The convoy will reach the port by midnight if the drivers ______ avoid the flooded road.
e: Do not use will or would in an if-clause; "if the drivers can avoid" expresses ability.

q: The first rural clinics here were paid for by Elias Cole, a retired ship captain. He spent his savings on six of them, and other donors soon copied him. According to this paragraph, ______.
o: a retired captain funded the earliest clinics
Cole worked as a doctor before he retired
the government paid for the first six clinics
no other donor ever gave money to a clinic
e: The text says a retired ship captain paid for the first clinics, and others copied him.

q: The first attempt failed, so the technician tried to start the old generator ______ with a fresh battery.
e: Again means one more time; ago, ever and since do not fit this sentence.

q: The captain decided to postpone the inspection. To postpone something means to ______.
o: move it to a later time
cancel it and never hold it
e: Postpone = delay something until a later time.

q: Because warm air ______, the top floor of the barracks is always the warmest place in winter.
e: Air is uncountable, and this is a general fact: use the simple present with -s (warm air rises).

q: Lieutenant Okafor had her laptop repaired at the computer shop on base. This means that ______.
o: a technician fixed it for her
she fixed it herself at the shop
she bought a laptop at the shop
she works as a repair technician
e: Have + object + past participle (had her laptop repaired): someone else does the job for you.

q: The new radio is very similar ______ the old model, so the operators learned to use it in one afternoon.
e: The adjective similar is followed by to: similar to something.

q: The backup generator doesn't run ______ as the new one, so we only use it in emergencies.
e: Not as + adverb + as compares two things: it doesn't run as quietly as the new one.

q: We drove past the training center ______ my father completed his basic training thirty years ago.
e: After a noun of place, where (= in which) introduces the relative clause.

q: On long highway trips, cruise control ______ the truck's speed, so the driver doesn't need to keep a foot on the gas.
e: Regulate = control something and keep it at the right level.

q: Private Mendoza is interested in ______ for the advanced English course at the base education center.
e: After a preposition such as in, use the -ing form: interested in applying.

q: The motor pool has far more vehicles to maintain this year ______ it had when I first arrived.
e: A comparison with more is completed with than (not then, which is about time).

q: Several pilots in our squadron enjoy ______ model airplanes in their free time.
e: Enjoy is followed by the -ing form: enjoy building.

q: Staff Sergeant Wu is ______ instructor in the battalion, so all the trainees hope to be in her group.
e: Superlative: the + adjective + -est (the friendliest). Never use most and -est together.

q: The duty officer stopped Private Hayes at the main gate. In other words, ______
o: Hayes was stopped by the duty officer.
The duty officer was stopped by Hayes.
Hayes will be stopped by the officer.
Hayes stopped the duty officer at the gate.
e: Passive: the object (Hayes) becomes the subject, then was + past participle + by + the person who did it.

q: I'll e-mail you the new duty roster as soon as the first sergeant ______ it.
e: After as soon as, when, before or after, use the simple present to talk about the future.

q: "Give me a ring when your flight lands, and I'll pick you up," Sergeant Price told me. He wants me to ______.
e: Give someone a ring (informal) = telephone someone.

q: If you can't call your family every week, at least try to call them ______; even a short call means a lot.
e: Occasionally = from time to time; it fits 'not every week, but at least now and then'.

q: Before the recruits arrived, the first sergeant had the old lockers ______ from the hallway.
e: Have + object + past participle (had the lockers removed): someone else did the work.

q: Something is wrong ______ the printer in the orderly room; it jams every time we print more than two pages.
e: Use wrong with: What's wrong with it? Something is wrong with the printer.

q: Airman Cole says the winter jacket he bought at the base exchange was a real bargain. He ______.
o: got it for a low price
e: A bargain is something you buy for less than its usual price.

q: Sergeant Torres met his future wife ______ a squadron picnic in San Diego.
e: Use at for events and gatherings: at a picnic, at a party, at a meeting.

q: You ______ check the tire pressure before you take the truck out on a long convoy.
e: Ought is always followed by to + base verb; should and must never take to.

q: Corporal Brandt ______ on four different vehicles since he joined the transportation company.
e: Since + a starting point in the past needs the present perfect; with he, use has + past participle.

q: This winter is ______ last winter, so the base has ordered extra fuel for the heaters.
e: Comparative of a short adjective: adjective + -er + than (colder than).

q: The supply clerk sorted the boxes by size and put them in neat rows on the shelves. She ______ them.
e: Arrange = put things in a particular order or position.

q: How long ______ to drive from the base to the international airport?
e: Simple present question: question word + does + subject + base verb (does it take).

q: Please don't ______ your coffee cup on top of the radio; it could spill into the controls.
e: Set (= put, place) takes an object: set a cup on the table. Sit takes no object.

q: If the platoon ______ better maps, it wouldn't have gotten lost during the night exercise.
e: Third conditional: if + past perfect (had had), then would have + past participle.

q: The three-hour delay at the airport didn't ______; they just played cards and waited calmly.
e: Word order: make + object + adjective (make the passengers angry).

q: Were the mechanics working on the truck when the fire alarm went off? ______
o: Yes, they were working on it.
Yes, they are working on it.
No, they were working on it.
Yes, they worked on the alarm.
e: A past continuous question (Were they working...?) takes a matching answer: Yes, they were working.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: Weren't the trucks inspected by the captain this morning?
Weren't inspected the trucks by the captain this morning?
Weren't the trucks this morning by the captain inspected?
The trucks weren't by the captain inspected this morning?
e: Negative passive question: Weren't + subject + past participle + by + agent + time.

q: The radio operator transmitted the new coordinates to the helicopter crews. In other words, she ______ them.
e: Transmit = send or pass something from one person or place to another.

q: The old track behind the gym isn't nearly as crowded ______ it was before the fitness center opened.
e: Not as + adjective + as: the second part of the comparison also uses as.

q: A life jacket ______, so it can hold an injured swimmer's head above the surface until help arrives.
e: Float = stay on the surface of the water instead of going down.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: Lieutenant Gray is looking forward to visiting her family.
Lieutenant Gray is looking to visiting forward her family.
Lieutenant Gray is visiting forward to looking her family.
Her family Lieutenant Gray is looking forward visiting to.
e: Look forward to + -ing: to comes right after forward, then the gerund and its object.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: We need someone reliable to watch the gate tonight.
We need reliable someone to watch the gate tonight.
We need someone to watch reliable the gate tonight.
We need to watch someone reliable the gate tonight.
e: An adjective comes after someone/something (someone reliable), then the infinitive (to watch).

q: The blue pickup in the parking lot belongs to my brother and me, so it's ______.
e: It belongs to my brother and me = it is ours (possessive pronoun, never with an apostrophe).

q: After the eruption, a river of ______ flowed down the mountain and covered the only road to the village.
e: Lava is the hot liquid rock that flows out of a volcano.

q: During the fire drill, the trainees left the building quickly through the emergency ______ at the end of the hall.
e: An exit is a door you use to leave a building.

q: The medic cut the soldier's sleeve open ______ a pair of scissors to reach the wound.
e: Use with for the tool you use: cut with scissors, open with a key.

q: After waiting an hour for the shuttle bus, Specialist Grant decided ______ a taxi to the airport.
e: Decide is followed by to + base verb: decided to take.

q: The coffee machine in the break room ______ repaired three times this month, and it still leaks.
e: Present perfect passive for a period up to now (this month): has been + past participle; singular subject, so has.

q: During a radio check, every station must ______ to the operator's call within ten seconds.
e: Respond to = answer or react to something (respond to a call, to an order).

q: The Parkers lived on Maple Street for twenty years, and all the families on ______ street came to their going-away party.
e: Use the for something already mentioned or known: the street = Maple Street.

q: ______ the captain nor his deputy was at the meeting, so the sergeant major took the notes.
e: Nor goes with neither: neither A nor B (= not A and not B).

q: The mechanics ______ working on the engine for six hours when they finally found the problem.
e: Past perfect continuous (had been + -ing): an action that continued up to a moment in the past.

q: The protocol office will make all the ______ for the general's visit, including hotels and transportation.
e: Make arrangements = plan and prepare the details (hotels, transportation, schedule).

q: My father ______ work the night shift at the airport, but now he has a regular day job.
e: Used to + base verb = a past habit or situation that is no longer true.

q: The pilot ______ land at the nearest airfield, or the plane will run out of fuel.
e: Have to = it is necessary; 'or...' shows what will happen if it is not done.

q: New drivers should ______ their mirrors every few seconds when they drive in heavy traffic.
e: After a modal (should, must, can...) use the base verb without to.

q: Carol Banks left her purse on a train. A conductor found it and gave it to station security, who returned it to her that evening. According to the text, she ______.
o: found a purse on a train
e: Security returned the purse to her the same evening, so she got it back.

q: Do you think the duty clerk would mind ______ these papers to the personnel office for me?
e: Mind is followed by the -ing form: would you mind taking...?

q: The traffic on the highway was bad this morning, but this evening it was even ______.
e: Bad, worse, the worst. Even + comparative: even worse.

q: As a boy, my brother always wished ______ a dog, but our apartment building didn't allow pets.
e: Wish for + noun = hope to get or have something.

q: My cousin cares only about expensive cars, designer clothes and the latest phones; she's very ______.
e: Materialistic = caring too much about money and possessions.

q: Traffic at Lakeside Airport has doubled in five years. The growth has brought jobs, but the airport can't hire mechanics fast enough, so some flights are canceled. The airport ______.
e: It cannot hire mechanics fast enough, so it does not have enough of them (it is short of mechanics).

q: As the only son, Marcus is the ______ to his grandfather's farm and will own it one day.
e: An heir is the person who will receive someone's property after that person dies.

q: According to the latest forecast, the storm ______ reach the coast early tomorrow, so all outdoor training is canceled.
e: Will + base verb for a prediction about the future (tomorrow).

q: "Does anyone else in your family serve in the military?" "______"
o: Yes, my sister is a Navy nurse.
Yes, I'm the only one who serves.
No, my brother is a Marine pilot.
Yes, my father works at a bank.
e: Anyone else asks about other family members, so the answer Yes must name another person who serves.

q: On our base, the post office is opposite the bank. This means the post office ______.
o: is across the road from the bank
is right next door to the bank
is on the top floor of the bank
is around the corner from the bank
e: Opposite = across from, facing it on the other side of the road.

q: Lieutenant Shaw is slowly getting used to living in Alaska. She ______.
o: lived in Alaska as a child
e: Get used to + -ing = become accustomed to something; do not confuse it with used to (a past habit).

q: After the long field exercise, the commander gave the battalion a three-day break ______ duty.
e: A break, holiday or rest from work or duty uses from.

q: Before the training course, most of the clerks had ______ experience with the new computer system.
e: Experience here is uncountable: use little (or much), not few, many or several.

q: Because of the snowstorm, the delivery truck ______ reach the base yesterday afternoon.
e: Past inability: couldn't + base verb (yesterday).

q: After ______ the safety briefing, the trainees put on their parachutes and boarded the plane.
e: After a preposition (after, before, by...) use the -ing form: after attending.

q: Airman Park isn't used to long night shifts. For him, working all night is ______.
e: Not be used to something = it is new or unfamiliar to you, so it feels strange.

q: The recruits had been waiting in line for an hour before the doors ______.
e: After before, use the simple past for the later event: the doors opened after they had been waiting.

q: "Does the cook prepare fresh bread every morning?" "Yes, she always ______ it before sunrise."
e: With she, he or it in the simple present, the verb takes -s: she always bakes.

q: On our base, the mail ______ every afternoon by a driver from the post office.
e: The mail receives the action, so use the passive: is/are + past participle (is delivered) + by + the doer.

q: The convoy drove ______ the coastal highway for three hours before it reached the port.
e: Along = following the length of a road, river or path.

q: Honey almost never spoils. Jars found in ancient tombs were still safe to eat after thousands of years. According to this paragraph, honey ______.
o: stays good for a very long time
goes bad within a few weeks
was never eaten by ancient people
must be kept in a freezer
e: Jars thousands of years old were still safe, so honey stays good for a very long time.

q: When the new barracks opened, it had beds for 200 recruits, but only 120 ever lived there. According to this paragraph, ______.
o: some of the beds stayed empty
the barracks was too crowded to use
the recruits preferred to sleep outside
e: There were 200 beds but only 120 residents, so many beds were never used.

q: The bridge over the creek is so narrow that ______.
o: only one truck can cross at a time
two trucks can cross at the same time
the creek is very deep in spring
drivers can park on both sides
e: So + adjective + that introduces a result: a very narrow bridge lets only one truck cross at a time.

q: The ______ report was kept in a locked safe in the colonel's office.
e: A past participle can work as an adjective before a noun: a classified (= secret) report.

q: By the time the firefighters arrived, the warehouse ______ by the flames.
e: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle, for an action finished before another past event.

q: ______ the entire convoy for a single broken headlight seems unreasonable to me.
e: A to-infinitive can be the subject of a sentence: To delay the convoy... seems unreasonable.

q: Please don't ______ those empty crates; we can reuse them to ship the spare parts.
e: Discard = throw away something you no longer need.

q: By Friday afternoon, the mechanics ______ every repair on the list, so the trucks were ready for Monday.
e: Past perfect (had completed) shows an action finished before a stated time in the past.

q: How ______ your sister like living in Germany?
e: How does + third-person subject + like...? asks for an opinion; do goes with I, you, we and they.

q: The new cook at the mess hall ______.
o: hasn't left the kitchen at all today
at all hasn't left the kitchen today
hasn't today left at all the kitchen
left hasn't the kitchen at all today
e: Normal order: auxiliary + not + past participle, then the object, then at all and the time word.

q: The cadet wore neither a belt nor suspenders with those baggy ______, so they kept slipping down.
e: Belts and suspenders hold up pants, so only pants fit the sentence.

q: A passenger asked, "Is this seat free?" He wanted to know if the seat was ______.
e: A free seat is one that nobody is using, so it is available.

q: The tent leaked badly during the storm, so tomorrow morning we will ______.
e: Choose the action that logically solves the problem: a leaking tent needs a patch.

q: Is Captain Hayes ______ his daughter to the airport tomorrow morning?
e: The present continuous (is + -ing) can express a planned future action: Is he taking...?

q: The soldiers were ready for ______ the cargo into the aircraft.
e: After a preposition such as for, use the -ing form: ready for loading.

q: The cadets stored ______ rifles in the armory before going to the mess hall.
e: Use a possessive adjective (their) before a noun; theirs stands alone without a noun.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: If the road is blocked, the convoy will take the northern route.
If the road will be blocked, the convoy will take the northern route.
If the road is blocked, the convoy would take the northern route.
If the road blocked is, the convoy will take the northern route.
e: First conditional: if + present simple, then will + base verb. Do not use will in the if-clause.

q: The driver turned on the headlights because ______.
e: A because-clause gives the logical reason: headlights are needed when it gets dark.

q: Even though the road was icy, the convoy reached the base on time. This means that ______.
o: the ice did not stop the convoy
the convoy was late because of the ice
the convoy waited for the ice to melt
the base was closed because of the ice
e: Even though introduces a contrast: the ice was a problem, but the convoy still arrived on time.

q: To assemble a tent single-handedly means to ______.
o: do it as quickly as possible
do it with a brand-new tool
do it only in good weather
e: Single-handedly = by yourself, without help from anyone else.

q: The ______ engine outside our window woke everybody up before dawn.
e: Use the -ing form as an adjective for something that is doing the action: a roaring engine.

q: Quiet, please! The general is ______ speak.
e: Be about to + base verb = be going to do something very soon.

q: The new tires ______ here by Thursday; otherwise, the truck can't join the convoy.
e: Should expresses what is expected: the tires should be here by Thursday.

q: Our company commander expects every soldier ______ the fitness test twice a year.
e: Expect + someone + to + base verb: expects every soldier to pass.

q: They teach basic navigation to every new cadet. This means that ______.
o: basic navigation is taught to every new cadet
every new cadet teaches basic navigation
basic navigation teaches every new cadet
basic navigation will be taught to every new cadet
e: Active to passive: the object becomes the subject, then is/are + past participle (is taught).

q: In the early days of flying, pilots had no instruments and navigated by looking at the ground. As planes flew higher and farther, engineers invented compasses, altimeters and radios. Which statement does the paragraph support? ______
o: Longer flights made new instruments necessary.
Early pilots found their way with radios.
Engineers stopped inventing after the compass.
Planes began to fly lower as instruments improved.
e: Planes flew higher and farther, and then engineers invented instruments: longer flights created the need for them.

q: Captain Stone has her uniforms cleaned at the base laundry. The uniforms are ______.
e: Have + object + past participle means someone else does the job for you: she has her uniforms cleaned.

q: The weather forecast for tomorrow looks ______ than today's; we can expect sunshine instead of rain.
e: The comparative of good is better (irregular); never gooder or more good.

q: The number of foreign students at the language school ______ risen sharply since January.
e: The number of + plural noun takes a singular verb, because the subject is the number: has risen.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: The sergeant wore a beautiful old silver watch.
The sergeant wore a silver old beautiful watch.
The sergeant wore an old silver beautiful watch.
The sergeant wore a beautiful silver old watch.
e: Adjective order: opinion (beautiful), then age (old), then material (silver), then the noun.

q: Bats are often shown as scary creatures in movies. In fact, most bats eat insects and are harmless to people. A single bat can catch thousands of mosquitoes in one night. According to this paragraph, bats ______.
e: A single bat catches thousands of mosquitoes in a night, so bats help control insects.

q: "The bus is leaving!" "Hang on a second! I'm ______."
e: Hang on = wait a moment; the speaker asks the others to wait because he is almost ready.

q: The printer wouldn't work yesterday, but the technician says it ______ work again tomorrow.
e: Will + base verb talks about the future (tomorrow); but shows the contrast with yesterday's problem.

q: The new cadets ______ the written exam last week because they were still in the field.
e: Past negative: didn't + base verb (didn't take); the main verb never takes the past form after didn't.

q: Corporal Shah would love ______ a quiet apartment off base.
e: Would like/love is followed by a to-infinitive: would love to rent.

q: Repairs on aircraft engines are usually done ______.
e: A hangar is the large building where aircraft are kept and repaired.

q: The soldiers use radios for ______ over long distances.
e: Radios are used for communication, which means passing messages to other people.

q: The engineers ______ the generator when the lights went out in the whole building.
e: Past continuous (were testing) describes an action in progress when another past action interrupted it.

q: The generator has been running ______ midnight, and it is almost out of fuel.
e: Use since with a point in time (since midnight) and for with a length of time (for six hours).

q: The company threw a small party in order ______ the new recruits feel welcome.
e: In order + to-infinitive expresses purpose: in order to make the recruits feel welcome.

q: We asked the technician ______.
e: Ask someone for something: the preposition for comes before the thing you request.

q: Hurricanes form over warm ocean water. When the water is hot enough, moist air rises quickly and begins to spin, and the winds grow stronger as the storm moves across the sea. According to this paragraph, a hurricane begins when ______.
o: warm, moist air rises and starts to spin
cold air from the north meets a mountain range
strong winds first reach the coast
heavy rain fills the rivers and lakes
e: The text says moist air rises and begins to spin over hot ocean water; that is how a hurricane starts.

q: When someone thanks you for holding the door, a polite reply is "______"
e: You're welcome is the standard polite answer to thank you.

q: The contractor violated the ______ when he used cheaper materials than the ones listed.
e: Violate a contract, rule or law = break it; using different materials breaks the contract.

q: ______ scissors are too dull to cut the thick cardboard.
e: Scissors is a plural noun (a pair of scissors), so use the plural demonstrative these.

q: Starting next month, ______ to arrive early at the training center?
e: A question with will: will + subject + base verb (will you try...?).

q: Pilots should avoid ______ over the storm area.
e: Avoid is followed by the -ing form: avoid flying.

q: The ______ equipment must be returned to the supply room by Friday.
e: A past participle can work as an adjective before a noun: borrowed equipment.

q: Private Ortega tried not to look ______ before the inspection, but his shaking hands showed how worried he was.
e: After the linking verb look (= seem, appear), use an adjective: look nervous.

q: The captain believed he should report the error immediately. This means that he felt ______.
o: it was his duty to report it
he could hide it for a while
he was unable to report it
it was too late to report it
e: Should expresses a duty: he believed he should report it = he felt it was his duty.

q: The doctor insisted ______ a full check-up before the pilot's next flight.
e: The verb insist is followed by the preposition on: insist on something.

q: Volunteers who ______ for the safety checks must sign this form before the exercise.
e: In a relative clause, use the verb be + adjective: who are responsible.

q: Rivera and Patel ______ the supply lists every Monday morning.
e: A compound subject (Rivera and Patel) takes a plural verb in the simple present: review.

q: Travel to the island is permitted ______ that visitors carry a valid permit.
e: Provided that = only if: travel is allowed on the condition that visitors carry a permit.

q: Early ships depended on the wind. Steam engines freed them from it, and nuclear power now lets some ships sail for years without refueling. According to this paragraph, some modern ships can sail for years because of ______.
e: The text says nuclear power lets some ships sail for years without refueling.

q: The pilot can ______ three languages fluently.
e: Speak a language is the fixed collocation; say, tell and talk need a different object.

q: What time does the flight to Denver ______?
e: Take off = leave the ground (said of a plane); the other combinations have different meanings.

q: The new employ______ was asked to sign the security form on her first day.
e: The suffix -ee names the person who receives or does something: employ + ee = employee.

q: If she lived closer to the base, she ______ walk to work every day.
e: Second conditional: if + simple past, then would + base verb.

q: The instructor showed my partner and ______ how to fold the parachute.
e: After a verb, use the object pronoun, even in a pair: showed my partner and me.

q: It was a quiet Sunday evening ______ the phone rang at the duty desk.
e: When introduces a clause about time: It was a Sunday evening when...

q: Firefighters check their gear every morning, even if there has been no ______ to fight for weeks.
e: Firefighters fight fires, so the logical word is fire.

q: Could you give me ______ information about the shuttle schedule?
e: Information is uncountable, so use some (not a, many or few).

q: The radar system detects approaching aircraft. In other words, ______.
o: approaching aircraft are detected by the radar system
approaching aircraft detect the radar system
the radar system is detected by approaching aircraft
the radar system was detected by approaching aircraft
e: Active to passive: the object becomes the subject, then are + past participle + by + the doer.

q: The cadets sang the national anthem ______ the opening of the sports festival.
e: Use at for events and ceremonies: at the opening, at a party, at a meeting.

q: The village ______ my grandfather was born no longer exists.
e: After a noun of place, where (= in which) introduces the relative clause.

q: Thunder is the sound made by lightning. A bolt of lightning heats the air around it so quickly that the air expands with a loud bang. According to this paragraph, thunder is caused by ______.
o: air expanding suddenly after it is heated
large clouds hitting each other in the sky
heavy rain falling on very hot ground
strong wind blowing through the mountains
e: The text says lightning heats the air so fast that it expands with a bang: that bang is thunder.

q: Preparing for a marathon is a slow process. Runners must increase their distance week after week and rest carefully to avoid injury. According to this paragraph, ______.
o: anyone can run a marathon without training
rest is not important for runners
e: Runners must increase distance week after week, so training for a marathon has to be gradual.

q: We reached the gate early because the ______ at the security checkpoint was short.
e: A short line (queue) means that few people are waiting.

q: Once the 20-minute equipment check is finished, the crew will start a 45-minute training flight. Which statement is true? ______
o: The check comes before the flight.
The flight is only 20 minutes long.
The flight begins before the check.
e: Once... is finished shows the order: first the equipment check, then the training flight.

q: The dockworkers stacked the ______ salmon in wooden crates before the trucks arrived.
e: A past participle can work as an adjective before a noun: smoked salmon (= salmon preserved with smoke).

q: Careful with that glass bottle. It ______ break if you drop it on the concrete floor.
e: Will + base verb predicts a certain result; ought to and has to express obligation, and can't has the opposite meaning.

q: What route is the convoy ______ tomorrow morning?
e: Present continuous question: is/are + subject + -ing (What route is the convoy taking?).

q: The residents were ordered ______ the area immediately because of the flood.
e: Order someone + to-infinitive; in the passive the to-infinitive stays: were ordered to evacuate.

q: The corridor was dim. It was ______.
e: Dim = not bright; a dim place has very little light.

q: The convoy drove through the night ______ dawn.
e: Until marks the time when an action stops: drove through the night until dawn.

q: Rivers change the land in two ways. Over thousands of years they cut deep canyons through solid rock, yet the soil they carry downstream also builds fresh land at their mouths. According to this paragraph, ______.
o: rivers can wear land away and build it
rivers only carry soil to the mountains
canyons are formed when soil builds up
rivers stop flowing when they reach rock
e: Rivers cut canyons (they remove land) and also build land with the soil they carry.

q: Call the clinic without delay. You should ______.
e: Without delay = immediately, so you should call right now.

q: The cat ______ the coffee table and landed on the sofa.
e: Jump over = go up and across an obstacle; landed shows that the cat was in the air.

q: The road was closed, so the drivers ______ to take another route.
e: Passive past: were + past participle. The drivers received the instruction, so use were told.

q: Please let me know if you hear ______ the personnel office before Friday.
e: Hear from someone = receive news or a message from them.

q: The helicopter may ______ if the fog gets any thicker.
o: not be able to take off
be not able to take off
not able be to take off
be able not to take off
e: After a modal, not comes first: may not be able to + base verb.

q: The radio in the truck is not working properly. This means that it ______.
e: Not working properly = not functioning correctly, so the radio has a problem.

q: "Wasn't the hike too hard for your father?" "Yes, but he finished it ______ his sore knee."
e: In spite of = despite: he finished the hike even though his knee hurt.

q: Be caut______ when you walk on the icy steps behind the barracks.
e: Cautious = careful to avoid danger; the suffix -ious forms adjectives.

q: The new program has produced no ______ results so far, only promises and reports.
e: Tangible results are real and can be seen or measured; here there are only promises.

q: A driver with good ______ vision can see a cyclist coming from the side without turning his head.
e: Peripheral vision is what you can see at the sides while looking straight ahead.

q: The expedition crossed vast tracts of unexplored ______ where no map had ever been drawn.
e: Wilderness = a large natural area where people have not settled or built anything.

q: Captain Ibrahim's favorite hobby is ______ old radios in his garage.
e: After the verb be, a gerund (-ing) can name an activity: his hobby is repairing radios.

q: I like jogging with Sergeant Brooks, so I often run with ______ before breakfast.
e: After a preposition (with) use an object pronoun: with him.

q: Our new truck can travel much farther ______ the old one on a single tank of fuel.
e: Use than to compare two things after a comparative: farther than.

q: It was freezing on the flight line, so Airman Petrov pulled a wool ______ down over his ears.
e: A wool hat is worn on the head and can cover the ears in cold weather.

q: Ruiz: Could the package have arrived yesterday? Chang: No, ______. The truck only left the depot this morning.
e: Past impossibility: couldn't have + past participle (couldn't have arrived).

q: My brother is taking an electronics course ______ the technical institute downtown.
e: Use at with a place where you study or work: at the technical institute.

q: The medal ______ to Staff Sergeant Mills by the colonel at yesterday's ceremony.
e: The medal receives the action, so the passive is needed: was presented (by the colonel).

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: The new recruits usually eat breakfast in the dining hall at six o'clock.
The new recruits eat usually breakfast in the dining hall at six o'clock.
The new recruits usually eat in the dining hall at six o'clock breakfast.
In the dining hall usually eat breakfast the new recruits at six o'clock.
e: A frequency adverb (usually) goes before the main verb; the place comes before the time.

q: Next month's training plan *includes* night navigation and first aid.
o: The soldiers will practice night navigation and first aid.
The soldiers have just finished night navigation and first aid.
The soldiers dislike night navigation and first aid.
The soldiers must choose between night navigation and first aid.
e: If a plan includes something, that thing is part of what is planned.

q: The paratroopers jumped from the plane at 3,000 meters. A few minutes later, they all came ______ safely in an open field.
e: Come down = move from a high place to a lower one, for example when landing from the air.

q: Private Evans challenged the base chess champion. He wanted to ______.
e: To challenge someone is to invite that person to compete against you.

q: ______ binoculars on the table belong to the night lookout, so leave them there.
e: Binoculars is a plural noun, so it takes the plural demonstrative These.

q: Everyone ______ wear a helmet on the obstacle course; otherwise, the instructor will stop the session.
e: Should shows what is necessary or advisable; the otherwise-clause gives the consequence.

q: The old generator has ______ since midnight, and the noise is keeping everyone awake.
e: Present perfect continuous: has / have + been + verb-ing (has been running).

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: The fastest way to reach the airport is to take the highway.
The fastest way the airport to reach is to take the highway.
To take the highway the fastest way is to reach the airport.
The airport reach to the fastest way is take to the highway.
e: Pattern: The fastest way to + verb is to + verb.

q: Every visitor to the supply depot must wear a badge. The badge has to be visible at all times, even in the cafeteria, because guards check IDs without warning. According to the paragraph, visitors should ______.
o: leave their badges at the gate
ask the guards for a new badge each day
e: The badge must be visible at all times, so visitors should keep it in view.

q: Radio operators use short code words to save time. The word 'roger', for example, means 'message received'. Many armies use the same code words, which helps soldiers from different countries work together. According to this paragraph, ______.
o: shared code words help armies work together
code words make radio messages much longer
each army keeps its code words secret from allies
radio operators rarely use code words
e: The paragraph says common code words help soldiers from different countries cooperate.

q: Corporal Reed crossed the shallow stream behind the camp on foot. The water was ______.
e: Shallow means not deep.

q: Before the army orders fifty radios, a few units will ______ a sample model in the field.
e: Try out = test something by using it before you decide to buy or keep it.

q: The guest speaker is a highly ______ engineer who has designed bridges on three continents.
e: A participle used as an adjective goes before the noun: a respected engineer is one that others respect.

q: Airman Fischer and Airman Okoro ______ the new software manual every evening.
e: A compound subject (A and B) is plural, so the verb has no -s: study.

q: ______ a sick soldier to stand guard duty in the cold was a serious mistake.
e: An infinitive phrase (To force ...) can be the subject of a sentence.

q: The dentist found a small ______ in my back tooth and said he would fill it today.
e: A cavity is a hole in a tooth caused by decay; a dentist fills it.

q: Basketball players rely on ______ vision to see teammates beside them while they keep their eyes on the ball.
e: Peripheral vision lets you notice things at the sides of your field of view.

q: Lieutenant Moreno *would like to* transfer to the flight school next year.
e: Would like to = want to; it is a polite way to say what you want.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: Would you please explain how to fill out this leave request?
How to fill out this leave request would you please explain?
Would you please explain this leave request how to fill out?
Would please you explain how to fill out this leave request?
e: Question order comes first (Would you please explain), then the embedded part: how to + verb + object.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: Let's take a short break after the drill.
Let's a short break take after the drill.
Let's take break a short after the drill.
Let's the drill after take a short break.
e: Let's + base verb + object: Let's take a short break.

q: Sergeant Kowalski has a short temper. He ______.
e: A short temper means a person gets angry quickly and easily.

q: There is still ______ soup in the pot if you are hungry.
e: Soup is uncountable, so use some (not a few, several or many).

q: The sergeant reported that the trucks *had already left* when the new order arrived. What does this mean?
o: The trucks left before the order came.
The trucks left after the order came.
The trucks never left the base.
The trucks will leave with the order.
e: Past perfect (had left) shows an action completed before another past event (the order arrived).

q: Radar is used for ______ aircraft that are too far away to be seen with the eye.
e: After a preposition (for) use a gerund: for detecting.

q: The radio battery was dead, ______ Specialist Park walked to the supply room for a new one.
e: So introduces a result: the battery was dead, so he went to get a new one.

q: Major Hale canceled the outdoor drill because ______.
o: the field was dry and firm
e: A drill is canceled for a bad reason such as dangerous weather; a thunderstorm is the only logical cause.

q: A blizzard shut down the highway for two days. The highway was closed by ______.
e: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with strong winds.

q: Liters and gallons are units used to measure the ______ of liquids such as fuel and water.
e: Liters and gallons measure volume, the amount of space a liquid takes up.

q: Because of the storm, our flight ______ have to be rescheduled for tomorrow.
e: Two modals cannot be used together; use modal + have to: might have to.

q: From now on, ______ to arrive at the formation five minutes early?
e: A question about the future uses question order: will + subject + base verb.

q: Which tools are the mechanics ______ on the generator today?
e: Are + subject + verb-ing makes a present continuous question: are the mechanics using.

q: The helicopter has been circling above the base ______ sunrise, and nobody knows why.
e: Since + a point in time (sunrise) goes with the present perfect continuous.

q: A recruit who refuses to listen to advice cannot improve. In other words, ______.
o: a recruit must accept advice to improve
a recruit who improves never needs advice
advice is useful only to the best recruits
an instructor must always listen to recruits
e: If refusing advice prevents improvement, then accepting advice is necessary to improve.

q: Some English expressions use colors. A person who is angry may be said to see red, someone who is sad feels blue, and a jealous person is green with envy. According to this paragraph, ______.
o: bright colors are liked by everyone
sad people often wear blue clothes
e: The examples show that English uses colors to stand for feelings.

q: A soldier who has a fractured wrist should ______.
o: get an X-ray at the clinic
carry a heavy pack as usual
e: A fractured wrist is a broken bone, so the soldier needs an X-ray and treatment at the clinic.

q: If the desert sand is scorching at noon, your feet will feel ______.
e: Scorching = extremely hot.

q: Please ______ the maps flat on the table so that everyone can see them.
e: Lay (lay, laid, laid) takes an object: lay the maps. Lie (lie, lay, lain) has no object.

q: The new rifle feels ______ the older model than I expected.
e: More like + noun = closer in nature or feel to that thing; alike cannot take an object.

q: Visitor passes ______ at the main gate between eight and five.
e: The passes receive the action, so use the passive: are issued.

q: The new barracks are comfortable in every way ______ the noise from the nearby runway.
e: Except for = not including; it names the one thing that is not comfortable.

q: Most people think the village well is about three hundred years old. Recent tests on its stones, though, suggest that it could be much older. According to the paragraph, the well ______.
o: may be older than people believed
is exactly three hundred years old
e: The tests suggest it could be much older, so the well may be older than people believed.

q: Don't ______ that broken radio; the technicians can use its parts to fix others.
e: Throw out = get rid of something you do not need or cannot use.

q: The rescue team ______ the small boat across the river with long wooden oars.
e: Row = move a boat through the water using oars.

q: The food at this base is much ______ than the food at my last assignment.
e: Use the comparative better with than; good has an irregular comparative.

q: We usually travel to the training area ______ truck, but today the whole company will march.
e: Use by + a means of transport without an article: by truck.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: The supplies should reach the camp before noon.
The supplies reach should the camp before noon.
The supplies should the camp reach before noon.
Noon the supplies before should reach the camp.
e: Word order: subject + modal (should) + main verb + object + time.

q: *Opening the crate slowly*, Corporal Lee found a note from the supply officer.
o: The supply officer opened the crate.
Someone else opened the crate for him.
e: A participle phrase at the start of a sentence describes the subject of the main clause: Corporal Lee.

q: Engineers needed almost three years to ______ the bridge across the river.
e: You build a bridge; the other verbs do not go with the object bridge.

q: Yesterday the ferry stayed in port because the crew ______ see the harbor entrance through the thick fog.
e: For a past situation use couldn't (= was not able to), not can't.

q: Thank you for not ______ your phone during the briefing.
e: After a preposition (for not) use a gerund: for not using.

q: Private Lang was ordered ______ his rifle to the armory after the drill.
e: Be ordered / told / instructed + to + base verb: was ordered to return.

q: The captain wants to meet Lieutenant Cruz and ______ at the gate before the inspection.
e: After the verb meet, use object pronouns: Lieutenant Cruz and me.

q: After an hour of testing, the technician still could not ______ why the circuit board kept overheating.
e: Figure out = understand or find the answer to a problem.

q: A funnel is used to ______ liquid into a bottle with a narrow opening.
e: A funnel guides liquid so that you can pour it into a small opening.

q: Every medic will gain a lot from the new trauma course. The course will be ______.
e: If people gain a lot from something, it is valuable (useful).

q: Wind turbines turn the movement of air into electricity. When the wind blows, the blades rotate and drive a generator. On calm days the blades hardly move, so very little power is made. According to this paragraph, a wind turbine ______.
o: burns fuel to run its generator
works best on very calm days
e: Turbines make little power on calm days, so they need wind to make electricity.

q: If the road had been open, the ambulance ______ have reached the village in time.
e: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

q: The mail ______ twice a day at the front desk.
e: The mail receives the action, so use the passive: is delivered.

q: Nadia: Have the new recruits received their uniforms? Tariq: Yes, ______.
e: A short answer repeats the auxiliary in its full form and is not contracted: Yes, they have.

q: What time ______ for the airport tomorrow morning?
e: Question word order: question word + auxiliary + subject + main verb.

q: The tailor measured every part of the recruit's body for the new uniform, including his chest, waist, and ______.
e: Shoulders are part of the body; sleeves, pockets and buttons belong to the uniform.

q: The mechanics worked ______ midnight to finish repairing the truck.
e: Until marks the time when an action stops: worked until midnight.

q: The old tent had so many holes that it was no longer ______, so we ordered a new one.
e: Usable = able to be used; a tent with many holes can no longer be used.

q: Since arriving at the training camp, Private Dalton has felt homesick. He ______.
e: Homesick = sad because you miss your home and family.

q: When the new hangar is finished next spring, the squadron ______ its helicopters there.
e: In a sentence about the future, the main clause takes will + base verb: will keep.

q: I would have called you earlier, ______ my phone battery died during the exercise.
e: Only used as a conjunction means but: it adds the fact that stopped the action.

q: The long briefing was not interesting at all. ______, half of the audience fell asleep.
e: In fact adds a stronger, more specific point to what was just said.

q: Camels can live in the desert for days without drinking. They store fat in their humps, and their bodies use it for energy when food is scarce. According to this paragraph, a camel's hump ______.
o: holds fat the animal can use
keeps the animal cool at noon
helps it to see at night
e: The paragraph says camels store fat in their humps and use it for energy.

q: It took Specialist Rao almost two weeks to get ______ the flu and return to duty.
e: Get over an illness = recover from it.

q: After the mechanics fixed the leak, the same problem ______ a week later.
e: Reappear = appear again after it had gone away.

q: Please bring the first-aid ______ quickly; Private Ward has cut his hand on the fence.
e: A first-aid kit is the box of supplies used to treat small injuries.

q: If the gym stayed open all night, more soldiers ______ use it after their shifts.
e: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb.

q: The plane is ______ take off, so please turn off your phones now.
e: Be about to + verb means something will happen very soon.

q: The doctor advised the patient ______ lifting heavy boxes for at least two weeks.
e: Advise + person + to + base verb: advised the patient to avoid.

q: Instead of ______ the highway, the convoy took the old river road to save fuel.
e: After a preposition such as "instead of", use the -ing form.

q: The soldiers call their old truck Big Bertha. In other words, the old truck ______ Big Bertha by the soldiers.
e: Passive voice: be + past participle (is called); the truck receives the action.

q: A battery works like a small storage tank. Just as a tank holds water until a faucet is opened, a battery holds energy until a circuit is closed. According to this paragraph, a battery ______.
o: keeps energy ready for later use
loses energy as soon as it is made
e: The text compares a battery to a tank: it stores energy until it is needed.

q: The instructor handed each cadet a pocket dictionary and said, "You may keep it." This means the cadets ______.
o: do not have to give it back
must return it by tomorrow morning
should never open it in class
have to pay for it first
e: "You may keep it" gives permission to keep it, so there is no need to return it.

q: The mechanic looked at the leaking hose and said, "You should replace this right away." He meant the owner should replace it ______.
e: Right away = immediately, without waiting.

q: The night march in the mountains was ______ exercise our company has ever done.
e: Use the most + a long adjective for the highest degree: the most exhausting.

q: By noon tomorrow, the survey team ______ in the desert for two full weeks.
e: Future perfect continuous (will have been + -ing) shows how long an action will have lasted by a future time.

q: The map in my old truck is badly out ______ date, so I always check the GPS.
e: Out of date is a fixed phrase meaning no longer current.

q: When the lights went out in the hallway, my first ______ was to reach for the flashlight.
e: A first reaction is what you do or feel immediately, before you think.

q: If you loosen this screw any further, the handle will probably ______.
e: When a screw is loosened, the part it holds can fall off.

q: Our radio operator is extremely reli ______; she has never lost a single message.
e: The adjective is spelled reliable (-able): it means "can be trusted".

q: My cousin likes to ______ about how fast he can run the obstacle course.
e: Boast about = talk with too much pride about what you can do.

q: Fixing the broken windows in the old barracks ______ going to take most of the week.
e: A gerund subject (Fixing...) takes a singular verb, even if a plural noun comes just before the verb.

q: It was ______ a hot afternoon that the colonel canceled the outdoor drill.
e: Use such + a + adjective + noun + that; so goes with an adjective alone (so hot that).

q: The news that the field exercise has been canceled is ______ to most of the trainees.
e: Use the -ing adjective for the thing that causes the feeling: the news is disappointing.

q: When I arrived at the depot, a number of trucks ______ already waiting in line.
e: A number of + plural noun takes a plural verb (were).

q: Sergeant Lopez did not attend the briefing, and Corporal Hale did not attend ______.
e: In a negative sentence put either at the end; too and also are used in positive sentences.

q: Either the lieutenant or her two assistants ______ responsible for locking the armory tonight.
e: After either...or the verb agrees with the noun closest to it: assistants are.

q: ______ the technician found inside the old radio amazed everyone in the repair shop.
e: What starts a noun clause used as the subject: What the technician found = the thing he found.

q: Corporal Alvarez ______ as an air traffic controller ever since he finished flight school.
e: Ever since + a past clause takes the present perfect in the main clause: has worked.

q: "Why is the report so late?" "You seldom finish your paperwork on time, ______ you?"
e: Seldom, rarely and hardly ever make a sentence negative, so the question tag is positive: do you?

q: Because of my new work schedule, I can only call my parents ______.
e: Say how often with number + a + period of time: twice a month.

q: The instructor made the cadets ______ the checklist aloud before every flight.
e: Make + object + base verb (no to): made the cadets read.

q: Lieutenant Cho has been waiting at the gate for over an hour, ______ she?
e: The question tag repeats the first auxiliary in the opposite form: has been... hasn't she?

q: The mechanics at our motor pool are very ______; they can repair a truck in half the usual time.
e: After "are very" use an adjective: efficient (not the noun or the adverb).

q: Recruits often have trouble ______ the radio codes during their first week of training.
e: Have trouble (or difficulty) + -ing: have trouble memorizing.

q: By the time the ambulance arrived, the medic ______ the bleeding already.
e: The past perfect (had + past participle) shows an action finished before another past action.

q: The graduation ceremony will take place ______ the afternoon of May 9, on the main parade field.
e: Use on with dates and with "the morning/afternoon of" a date.

q: The cook spent most of the morning ______ vegetables for the field kitchen.
e: Spend time + -ing: spent the morning peeling.

q: It took the maintenance crew almost three days ______ the broken water main.
e: It takes + person + time + to + base verb.

q: After a month of training, Private Santos shoots much ______ than she did on the first day.
e: The comparative of well is better; do not say "more good".

q: You had better ______ the oil level before you start the long drive tomorrow.
e: Had better is followed by the base form of the verb, without to.

q: The shuttle bus isn't running today, so ______ a taxi to the airport.
e: Use will ('ll) for a decision made at the moment of speaking.

q: Of the four pilots in our squadron, Captain Ortiz is ______ experienced.
e: Use the most + adjective to compare one person with three or more others.

q: ______ the store advertised a big sale, only a few customers came in on Saturday.
e: Although shows a contrast and is followed by a full clause; despite needs a noun or an -ing form.

q: "Do you want to take the bus or walk to the base?" "I prefer walking ______ riding the bus."
e: Prefer X to Y: prefer walking to riding (not "than").

q: After the doctor's warning, Dad finally stopped ______ sugar in his coffee.
e: Stop + -ing means quit an activity; stop + to + verb means pause in order to do something.

q: The flight will leave on time unless the fog ______ worse before noon.
e: After if and unless use the present simple for a future event: unless the fog gets worse.

q: "Do you know how you will get to the airport?" "Not yet. I think I ______ Sergeant Bell for a ride."
e: Use will for a decision you are making as you speak: I think I will ask.

q: Hurry, Corporal! How ______ time do we have before the briefing starts?
e: Time is uncountable, so ask How much time...?

q: Captain, how long ______ at the north checkpoint yesterday morning?
e: In a past simple question use did + subject + base verb: did the convoy wait.

q: The pilot ______ a little worried when I talked to him last night.
e: Use the past simple (seemed) for a finished time; seem is not used in the continuous form.

q: The workshop is closed this morning because there is no ______ in the building.
e: Electricity is uncountable: it has no plural and no a/an.

q: We packed two radios for the hike. The first has a weak battery, but ______ works perfectly.
e: When only two things are mentioned, the second is called the other.

q: Please ______ touch the exhibits in the museum; some of them are very old.
e: A negative request is formed with Please don't + base verb.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: Has your brother ever flown in a helicopter?
Your brother has ever flown in a helicopter?
Has ever your brother flown in a helicopter?
Does your brother ever flown in a helicopter?
e: In a present perfect question the auxiliary comes first: Has + subject + ever + past participle.

q: Would you mind ______ the lights off when you leave the barracks tonight?
e: Would you mind is followed by an -ing form: Would you mind turning...?

q: The shelter was full when we arrived, and now we have nowhere to sleep. We ______ have called ahead.
e: Should have + past participle expresses regret about something you did not do.

q: I found your keys in the hallway this morning. I will ______ at lunch.
e: When the direct object is a pronoun, it comes first: bring them to you.

q: Applicants may ______ their forms online or at the front desk of the education center.
e: After a modal verb (may, can, must) use the base form: may submit.

q: The technician opened the old radio and ______ removed the damaged circuit board.
e: An adverb (carefully) describes a verb; careful is an adjective.

q: Lieutenant Gray is ______ duty this weekend, so she cannot come to the picnic.
e: Use on in fixed expressions such as on duty, on leave and on vacation.

q: We can't make breakfast for the whole platoon; there are too ______ eggs in the supply tent.
e: Eggs are countable, so use too few; too little and too much go with uncountable nouns.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: She admitted that she had forgotten the password.
She admitted she that had forgotten the password.
That she admitted had forgotten she the password.
The password she that admitted had forgotten.
e: In a that-clause keep statement order: that + subject + verb + object.

q: Before driving over the mountain pass in winter, always put chains on the ______.
e: Snow chains are fitted around the tires so that the vehicle can grip icy roads.

q: If you have a headache, you could take some ______ and rest for an hour.
e: Aspirin is a medicine you swallow to reduce pain.

q: The patient was lying ______ a thin sheet because the room was warm.
e: Under means covered by something; here the thin sheet is the cover.

q: She had been ______ her retirement for years when the offer finally came.
e: Past perfect continuous: had been + verb with -ing.

q: On their day off, Sergeant Mbeki and his wife like to go ______ in the mountains.
e: Go + -ing is used for activities: go hiking, go fishing, go swimming.

q: The whole crowd started cheering ______ the band walked onto the stage.
e: As soon as links two events that happen one right after the other.

q: Be careful with that knife! Last week Corporal Diaz cut ______ while he was opening a box.
e: Use a reflexive pronoun (himself) when the object is the same person as the subject.

q: Clothes that do not fit properly are usually altered by ______.
e: A tailor makes clothes and changes them to fit a person.

q: A deep, narrow valley with steep rock walls, often cut by a river, is called a ______.
e: A canyon is a deep valley with steep sides, usually shaped by a river.

q: The circumference of the running track at our base is a little over ______.
e: Circumference is the distance around a circle or track, so it is measured in miles, meters or feet.

q: Owls hunt mostly at night. Their large eyes gather even the faintest light, and their soft feathers let them fly almost without a sound. According to this paragraph, owls ______.
o: have trouble seeing in the dark
e: Soft feathers let owls fly almost without a sound, so they can hunt without being heard.

q: Every spring the airport replaces its shuttle buses. The school district buys the old ones cheaply, paints them yellow and uses them to carry students. According to the paragraph, ______.
o: the school district reuses old airport buses
the airport buys more buses every month
students ride to the airport every spring
the airport paints its buses yellow
e: The district buys the airport's old buses and uses them for students.

q: Of all the trucks in the motor pool, this one uses ______ fuel.
e: Use the least with an uncountable noun like fuel when you compare more than two things.

q: ______ are you going to say to the colonel about the broken radio?
e: Say needs an object, so the question word must be What.

q: If Sergeant Diaz ______ here, he would know how to fix this radio.
e: In an unreal present condition, use were after if and would in the main clause.

q: When ______ the fire alarm go off in the barracks last night?
e: Past simple questions use did + the base verb (go).

q: I wish my brother ______ come to my graduation, but he is stationed overseas.
e: After wish, use could for something that is not possible now.

q: Every morning at six, the gate to the training area ______ by the first guard on duty.
e: The gate does not open itself: use the passive (is opened) with by.

q: My grandmother ______ most of her childhood on a farm in Kansas.
e: We spend time: she spent her childhood on a farm.

q: Who built the footbridge behind the hospital? It ______ by army engineers two summers ago.
e: A passive sentence needs was + past participle, with by for the doer: it was built by army engineers.

q: My flight lands at six, so my brother will be ______ at the arrivals gate with a sign when I come out.
e: After will be, use the -ing form (future continuous): he will be waiting.

q: The small town ______ my grandmother grew up has only one traffic light and a single gas station.
e: After a noun of place, where (= in which) begins the clause: the town where she grew up.

q: My grandparents have lived ______ Willow Street since 1985, and they know every neighbor by name.
e: Use on with the name of a street (on Willow Street); at is for a full address with a number.

q: The sergeant got the new recruits ______ their boots before the inspection, and the whole platoon looked sharp.
e: Get + person + to + base verb means cause someone to do something: got the recruits to polish.

q: I'm not sure whether the package arrived today. The courier ______ have left it at the front desk.
e: May have + past participle expresses a possibility about the past; maybe is an adverb, not a modal verb.

q: The recruiting office is ______ 450 Harbor Road, right next to the fire station.
e: Use at with a complete street address that has a number: at 450 Harbor Road.

q: The mail truck ______ the main gate only a few minutes ago, so the packages should reach the post office soon.
e: Ago points to a finished time in the past, so use the simple past (left), not the present perfect.

q: Our unit saves a lot of fuel by ______ the engines during long waits at the checkpoint.
e: After the preposition by, use the -ing form: by turning off the engines.

q: The cook says there is plenty left, so I'll take ______ more chili with my cornbread.
e: Chili is uncountable, so use a little; a few, many and a couple of go with plural countable nouns.

q: Always wear hearing protection near the jet engines; ______, you could damage your ears permanently.
e: Otherwise means 'if you do not do this': it introduces the bad result of ignoring the instruction.

q: Corporal Lee is a night owl, so he ______ goes to bed before midnight.
e: Seldom means rarely, which fits a night owl; ever cannot be used in a plain positive statement like this.

q: After the range closed for repairs, the clerk amended the training schedule. In other words, she ______ it.
e: Amend = change a document, such as a schedule or an order, to correct or improve it.

q: Sergeant Ruiz wrote down the odometer reading before the convoy left. She wanted to record ______.
o: the distance the truck had traveled
the highest speed the truck reached
the amount of fuel in the tank
e: An odometer shows how far a vehicle has traveled; a speedometer shows speed and a gauge shows fuel.

q: The panel of three doctors ______ every patient carefully before deciding on any treatment.
e: The subject is the singular noun panel (not doctors), so the present simple verb takes -s: examines.

q: "You'd better go over the route one more time," the convoy commander told Sergeant Moore. The commander wants him to ______.
e: You'd better = it is a good idea to; go over something = check or review it carefully.

q: Private Novak stuffed ______ that he could not zip it.
o: so many clothes into his bag
clothes so many into his bag
so clothes many into his bag
many so clothes into his bag
e: Word order: so + many/much + noun, then the place phrase (so many clothes into his bag).

q: Several cadets in my class have become very interested ______ photography since the visit to the art museum.
e: The adjective interested is followed by the preposition in: interested in photography.

q: "Should I bring a flashlight on the night hike?" "______"
o: Yes, it gets very dark out there.
No, I already had dinner at the club.
Yes, the hike starts at noon.
No, I like the quiet in the morning.
e: Only this reply answers the question: you need a flashlight because it gets dark on a night hike.

q: "Can the height of this chair be adjusted?" "______"
o: Yes, pull the lever under the seat.
No, it was delivered on Tuesday.
Yes, it is the same color as the desk.
No, the office closes at five.
e: Adjust = change something a little to fit your needs; only the first reply explains how to do that.

q: Although the old truck is slow, it is very reliable. In other words, the truck ______.
e: Although introduces a contrast: the truck is slow, but it can be trusted.

q: Where can I get ______ ink for this printer? The cartridge has been empty since yesterday.
e: Ink is uncountable, so use some; a, one and many cannot be used before it.

q: The battalion will hold a short award ceremony ______ the final inspection on Friday afternoon.
e: After + noun phrase = later than that event; when needs a clause, and since does not fit a future plan.

q: A hospital emergency room is usually very ______ on Saturday nights, with doctors rushing from patient to patient.
e: Hectic = very busy, with a lot of activity and little time to rest.

q: The printer jammed last Tuesday, and the office has been using the old copier ______ then.
e: Since + a point in time (since then) goes with the present perfect; for is used with a length of time.

q: The new identification cards will be ______ to every recruit before the end of the week.
e: Future passive: will be + past participle; the past participle of send is sent.

q: After the festival, the prize money was divided ______ all fifty members of the volunteer team.
e: Use among for more than two people or things; between is for two.

q: When rainwater freezes on a road at night, it forms a thin, dangerous layer of ______.
e: Water that freezes turns into ice; steam and fog are vapor, and mud is soil mixed with water.

q: The old sergeant cooks dinner for ______ and his two grandchildren every Sunday.
e: When the object of a preposition is the same person as the subject, use a reflexive pronoun: for himself.

q: I have two bags for the trip. The blue bag is much ______ than the green bag, so I will carry the green bag.
e: A short adjective ending in -y forms its comparative with -ier (heavier), followed by than.

q: Visitors must ______ at the main gate before they enter the base.
e: A modal verb such as must is followed by the base form without to: must sign in.

q: Choose the correct sentence: ______
o: Did the mechanic return the keys to the sergeant before lunch?
Did return the mechanic the keys to the sergeant before lunch?
Did the mechanic the keys return to the sergeant before lunch?
Did before lunch the mechanic return the keys to the sergeant?
e: A past simple yes/no question has the order Did + subject + base verb + object + other information.

q: The doctor ______ me last Friday that I should rest for a week before returning to duty.
e: Last Friday is a finished time in the past, so use the simple past (told), not the present perfect.

q: Everyone in my unit ______ take a fitness test twice a year.
e: Has to + base verb expresses a requirement; wants, ought and is able all need to before the verb.

q: Never send a text message while ______ a truck on the base roads.
e: After while, use the -ing form when the subject is the same: while driving.

q: The general wanted the engineers ______ the bridge before the rainy season began.
e: Want + object + to + base verb: wanted the engineers to finish.

q: The recruits ______ arrive on time every morning, or they will lose their weekend passes.
e: Must expresses a strong obligation, and the or-clause gives the result of not obeying; may, might and can do not.

q: The radio was so old and noisy that it was very hard to ______.
e: A noisy radio is hard to listen to; the other verbs do not fit a radio.

q: Compared with the old version, the new software seems ______ much faster.
e: Seem is followed by to + base verb: seems to load.

q: To protect the batteries, operators should avoid ______ the radio on all night.
e: Avoid is followed by the -ing form: avoid leaving.

q: The medical team ______ of two doctors, four nurses and a pharmacist.
e: Consist of is used in the active simple present (the team consists of...), never in the passive or continuous.

q: Please ______ all the doors and windows before you leave the building tonight.
e: A polite command uses please + the base form of the verb: Please lock...
